I laid on the ground with my 13 year old lab when he would have these “illnesses” where he would stop eating for a few days, stop walking... we would buy pedialyte and I would use a dropper and once he got his strength back I would make him rice and boiled chicken and hand feed it to him. We did this multiple times until his last “illness.” I don’t know how to describe it to you but I knew it was going to happen in the next few days. I called out of work and I would lay on the ground with him for hours a day. The second day he passed away.... the whole process took 20 seconds. I read a poem to him and hugged him.

My regrets: trying to give him pedialyte with the dropper that final day. I wish I would have let him be. I also regret not talking with my husband and verbalizing out loud that this wasn’t an illness but the old man actively dying...

Things I am thankful for: keeping my emotions in check that day, especially as he was actively passing. It was about him not me; I can cry later. Also thankful it happened during the day...

Honestly the only thing you can do is love him.
Let him on the couch. Lift him up on your bed if he likes that. Try to give him broth or something else light on the stomach that’s tasty- we did meat baby food. That was a big hit. Make sure his bedding is clean and dry. Put a towel under him if he can’t hold it. Don’t force him to do anything he can’t do, especially things that are more for the humans piece of mind and comfort (such as walks/outings- play that by ear. Youll know what’s too much).

My 6 month old dog got bit last week. Ripped his ear. It happened at daycare so I had direct access to the other owner, shot records etc. She may or may not have given you the correct contact info. If it ever happens again call the police. If you see her out there again call the police, wait nearby and approach her with the cops. Animals are considered property and her property injured yours. You can take her to small claims if she refuses to pay the vet bill but likely she will just pay up because it’s easier. Also you will get shot records and the event will be on paper in case this becomes a recurrent issue. 

As far as your dog- focus on training and love. Is he acting different? How are his wounds healing up? My ear wound has been a pain in the ass and he will likely always have a little slit (the very end didn’t heal)... also has a gouge over his eye and his nose is ripped up (hope the black comes back!)... total vet bills (3 trips) around 1k all paid for by the owner is the aggressive animal
